title: Deploying the cockpit
text:
The site is fully static — no server, no database, no Node build. Everything the browser needs is web/_site/ after a render.


# from the project root, with data/*.rds up to date
Rscript -e 'source("R/web/build_web_bundle.R"); build_web_bundle()'
quarto preview web



Rscript R/pipeline/data_pipeline_espn.R          # refresh espn_db (edit season/week in config/config.yml)
Rscript R/decision/decision_pipeline.R           # or source() + run_decision_pipeline(...)
Rscript -e 'source("R/web/build_web_bundle.R"); build_web_bundle(privacy = "public")'
quarto render web                                # -> web/_site/
privacy = "public" drops owner_name / owner ids. Use "private" (the default) only for a deploy that is not world-readable.
Then serve web/_site/ from anywhere:
python3 -m http.server -d web/_site 8000        # or any static host



web/data/ is gitignored and data/*.rds never leaves the machine, so Pages cannot build the bundle in CI. Publish the rendered output from your machine:
quarto publish gh-pages web
This renders and pushes web/_site/ to the gh-pages branch of origin (DudesFantasyApp). Enable Pages for that branch in the repo settings. A private repo’s Pages site is still world-readable unless you are on a plan with private Pages — treat it as public and always publish with privacy = "public".



Upload the contents of web/_site/ as a static site (direct upload, not a Git build). Same privacy = "public" rule applies for any world-readable host.



Plotly and DuckDB-Wasm load from jsDelivr at runtime (see web/js/head.html), so the published site needs network access on first load. To make it fully offline, vendor them under web/vendor/ — see web/vendor/README.md.



ESPN cookies (config/config.yml, R/api/example_espn_342842788.R) or any data/*.rds. The bundle build only ever reads them; validate_web_bundle() and tests/web/test_privacy_public.R guard the output.
